key.name: enabled
key.description: Master toggle for showing the overlay button and layout popup on each window.

key.name: gap-px
key.summary: Gap between tiled windows in pixels
key.description: Defaults to 0 (windows snap edge-to-edge, seamlessly, like Windows' own Snap). Raise this if you'd rather have a visible gap between tiled windows.

key.name: button-hit-size-px
key.description: Size of the Shell-drawn button shown next to each window's own maximize button; clicking it opens the layout popup.

key.name: app-extra-clearance-overrides
key.description: List of "wmclass=extra_px" pairs. Some apps draw more than the standard minimize/maximize/close 3-button cluster in their header bar (VS Code's layout toggles, a browser's own Share button, etc.), so the overlay button needs extra clearance on top of the generic estimate to avoid landing on top of them. Matched case-insensitively as a substring of the window's WM_CLASS. A small built-in table covers a few common apps; entries here take priority over it and let you add more.

key.name: button-position-fractions
key.summary: Per-app horizontal position of the overlay button within the title bar
key.description: Maps a window's WM_CLASS (lower-cased) to the fractional horizontal position (0.0 = left edge, 1.0 = right edge) the user last dragged that app's overlay button to within its title bar. An app with no entry here uses the automatic placement next to its window controls. Keyed per app specifically so dragging the button on one application's window never moves the button on a different application's window.

key.name: snap-assist-enabled
key.summary: Offer other open windows for the remaining zones after a snap
key.description: Matches Windows 11's Snap Assist: after snapping a window into one zone of a multi-zone layout, highlights the still-empty zone(s) directly on screen with the user's other open windows on the same workspace offered as clickable choices to fill them.
